records.issue_text: [BUG] getForLogin calls IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(String) and a six-argument constructor (loaded, cacheKey, realm, searchKey, cached, parentQuery) that do not exist on the existing IdentityProviderListQuery class in this module. The `idp-alias-20` broker created in step 1 leaks into the realm after the test (and the cleanup lambda targets a non-existent `"alias"` provider), so subsequent tests in the same realm see a stale keycloak-oidc broker with BROKER_PUBLIC set.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The re-added `idp.isEnabled()` filter, commented as needed because 'idp might have been wrapped', is a symptom patch for the cache provider's createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel wrapper dropping/garbling the enabled flag, smuggled into a PR whose stated scope is caching. Any future caller of getForLogin that does not independently re-check isEnabled() (e.g. new login pages or API endpoints) will render disabled IDPs as clickable login options whenever the org-aware wrapper is in play; the invariant 'getForLogin only returns enabled IDPs' is enforced by post-filtering at one call site instead of in the wrapper or the cache provider, which is the next change that gets riskier because of this.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path in getForLogin builds the result from session.identityProviders().getById(id) without applying createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, while both the cache-miss path and the null-idp fallback path do apply it, so the same logical call returns differently-wrapped models depending on whether the list cache was warm. Organization-aware login pages get raw IdentityProviderModel instances on cache hits but wrapped ones on misses; any behavior the wrapper adds (e.g., hiding the IDP from non-org contexts or altering its displayed alias/config) silently differs between requests, and the re-check of isEnabled() in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean hints the wrapper already changes semantics that this path loses.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache key cacheKeyForLogin omits organizationId, so each distinct organizationId for the same FetchMode evicts the previously cached searchKey: the query!=null branch calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey) and rebuilds, discarding the other organization's cached result set. Realms with multiple organizations (the core use case of ALL/ORG_ONLY fetch modes) thrash the shared cache entry per organization, degrading to repeated delegate round-trips; in a cluster, concurrent requests for different orgs repeatedly invalidate each other's entries.
records.rationale: `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` is only `realmId + ".idp.login." + mode` (no `organizationId`). In `getForLogin`, when a different `organizationId` (i.e., different `searchKey`) is requested and `query.getIDPs(searchKey)` returns null, the code explicitly does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and rebuilds the cached entry. records.issue_text: [BUG] The cache-hit path of getForLogin resolves models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and never applies createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel, so cache hits and cache misses return differently-shaped IdentityProviderModel objects. The cache-miss/isInvalid branches wrap every delegate result with this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (organization-aware enable/disable semantics), but the cached branch returns raw models from getById. A user hitting the login page after the list query is cached gets unwrapped models, producing different visibility/enablement behavior than the first, uncached request — the exact class of bug the freemarker isEnabled re-check in this same diff papers over, meaning the cached path can list IDPs on the login page that the uncached path would have hidden.
